findings.current: Sometimes, your true feelings just don’t get through to the other person.
findings.defect: The Korean explicitly says “my true feelings,” but the translation shifts to a generic second-person viewpoint.
findings.rationale: The source uses 내 진심, preserving the narrator’s first-person perspective.
findings.replacement: Sometimes, my true feelings just don’t get through to the other person.

findings.current: The more I thought about it, the stranger it seemed.
findings.defect: The source says the more one knows or learns, the stranger it is; the translation changes that accumulating knowledge into thinking about it.
findings.rationale: 알면 알수록 means “the more one knows,” not “the more one thinks about it.”
findings.replacement: The more I learned, the stranger it seemed.

findings.current: So don’t do anything stupid like fighting to the death.
findings.defect: “Fighting to the death” implies the fight will end in death, stronger than the source’s warning not to risk one’s life fighting.
findings.rationale: 목숨 걸고 싸우다 means to fight while risking one’s life; it does not necessarily mean fighting until someone dies.
findings.replacement: So don’t do anything stupid like risking your life in a fight.

summary: The translation is largely faithful, with a few shifts in viewpoint and meaning.
